cards.hearing: You may hear that oil prices jumped overnight on reports that the White House is weighing possible strikes on Iran, with the news landing right before the midterm elections.
cards.why: Oil is the raw material behind gas and diesel, so when it jumps, truckers and shippers can feel it first, and that cost has a way of showing up later in what things cost at the store.
cards.but: But a single overnight headline about a possible strike is not the same as a policy that has actually happened, and markets often react before anything is confirmed.
cards.story: Picture a driver who hears a siren three blocks away and immediately detours the whole trip. Most of the time the siren has nothing to do with their route. We wait to see what is actually happening before we change direction.
say: We see the headline, and we are not reacting to a maybe.
One overnight story on oil does not rewrite a long-term plan.
